moat_against: Inverse condemnation: liable for equipment-caused fires without proof of negligence — the tail that bankrupted the equity in 2019-20
CPUC caps allowed ROE — no pricing power; affordability-first politics in the 2027-2030 general rate case
Debt-funded growth: net debt $57,495M at YE2025 and rising ($4.4B of Utility bonds issued in H1 2026); equity absorbs any disallowance first
Continuation Account is authorized, not pre-funded cash — IOU contributions run 2029-2045 while the original Wildfire Fund is being drawn by Eaton Fire claims
Diluted share count creeping up ~1.1%/yr (engine share CAGR), a small per-share drag
moat_for: Legal-monopoly electric/gas franchise across Northern/Central California — essential service, inelastic demand, no switching
Visible growth: $73B capex plan through 2030, FY2026 core EPS guided $1.64-$1.66, >=9% core EPS growth targeted through 2030, no new equity required
Diablo Canyon nuclear — scarce carbon-free baseload asset with renewed license
12+ GW data-center project pipeline — real load-growth optionality
SB 254 (signed Sep 2025) adds an $18B Wildfire Fund Continuation Account; PG&E 2026 disallowance cap ~$5.1B
moat_justification: Legal-monopoly electric and gas franchise across Northern and Central California (~16 million people, essential inelastic demand) with unusually visible growth: a $73B capital plan through 2030, FY2026 core EPS guided to $1.64-$1.66 and at least 9% core EPS growth targeted through 2030 with no new equity, the scarce Diablo Canyon nuclear plant, and a 12+ GW data-center pipeline. Capped at 5 because the CPUC sets allowed returns (no pricing power), growth is debt-funded (net debt $57,495M), and California inverse condemnation leaves an equity-killer wildfire tail — the 2019-20 bankruptcy is the proof; SB 254's $18B Continuation Account (signed Sep 2025, PG&E disallowance share 47.85%, ~$5.1B 2026 disallowance cap) softens but does not remove it, and IOU contributions do not run until 2029-2045.
name: PG&E Corporation
one_liner: Regulated California monopoly with a binary wildfire tail, moat 5/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 years (capex exceeds OCF every year; normalized base -$1.46/share) — Tier F on this screen; guided ~9-10% core EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
